AUDIT_F3.title: Partial instrument failure durability

task1_multiInstrumentPartialFailure.construction: Two fresh, unrelated single-section credit agreements (Restricted Payments $12M / Asset Sales $9.5M - deliberately different covenant families/amounts than Workstream H's own Indebtedness/Liens fixtures) that package-graph genuinely resolves into two SEPARATE standalone instruments (confirmed empirically in the test, not assumed).
task1_multiInstrumentPartialFailure.injectionMethodDifference: Workstream H's own test injects the failure via lib/contract-model/analysis/semantic-truth/service.ts's persistSemanticTruthForInstrument. This recertification deliberately injects at a DIFFERENT, LATER stage instead - lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-coverage/pipeline.ts's runSemanticCoverageAudit, which has no internal per-instrument fault isolation of its own - to independently test whether the fix's durability boundary is a genuine wrap around the WHOLE analyzeInstrument call (as orchestrator.ts's own code shows) or was narrowly coupled to the one function Workstream H's own test happened to mock.
task1_multiInstrumentPartialFailure.resultA_failingIssueDurable: CONFIRMED - reload from Postgres shows exactly 1 AnalysisRunIssue row for the failing instrument, documentIds correct, errorClass 'Error', message containing the real injected marker, failedStage 'PER_INSTRUMENT_ANALYSIS'.
task1_multiInstrumentPartialFailure.resultB_succeedingInstrumentPreserved: CONFIRMED, and additionally strengthened: because this recertification's injection point is LATER in the per-instrument sequence than persistence, it also independently proves that instrument B's OWN already-computed semantic-truth rows (persisted before the injected coverage-audit failure) are NOT rolled back or discarded even though B's own outcome never reaches instrumentOutcomes - a stronger, more adversarial proof of 'already-computed valid claims are never discarded' than testing at the persistence stage alone, since it shows partial-within-instrument work survives, not just whole-other-instrument work.
task1_multiInstrumentPartialFailure.resultC_statusGenuinelyPartial: CONFIRMED - result.status and the RELOADED persistedRun.status are both exactly 'PARTIAL', never 'COMPLETED' or 'COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW'.

task2_totalFailureAllInstrumentsRecorded.construction: Same two-instrument package, coverage-audit stage forced to fail unconditionally for both.
task2_totalFailureAllInstrumentsRecorded.result: CONFIRMED - result.status/persistedRun.status both 'FAILED' (never 'PARTIAL', preserving the genuinely-fatal-whole-run semantics). Exactly 2 AnalysisRunIssue rows exist (one per document/instrument), both containing the injected marker - i.e. the pre-AUDIT-F3 bug (only the FIRST error's message folded into fatalError, the rest silently discarded) does not reappear at this alternate injection point either.

task1_realClickPathTrace.finding: The 'confirmedBypass' 15-live-product-flow.json itself found was NOT eliminated - only made visible. app/[companyId]/onboarding/documents/page.tsx still renders an UNCONDITIONAL `<Link href={`/${companyId}/onboarding/review`}>Continue to Review</Link>` with no gate, disabled state, confirmation step, or reference to AnalysisRun/analysis status anywhere near it (statically confirmed by a fresh test that parses the real, current file and checks the ~400 characters immediately preceding the href for any such guard token - none exists). task1_realClickPathTrace.designJudgmentReassessed: 15-live-product-flow.json's own 'designJudgment' reclassifies this from a bug into an accepted two-step design 'AS LONG AS the product's own status model makes the uploaded-vs-analyzed distinction real and visible' - and then implements ONLY the visibility half, leaving the actual bypass the audit finding's own requiredOutcome names ('a real user cannot reach the product's analyzed state without the authoritative contract-analysis path having run') genuinely unresolved. This context does not change the disposition (the audit finding's own stated requiredOutcome is about the contract-model path specifically, and that path remains bypassable exactly as found), but is disclosed so the STILL_OPEN verdict is not read as 'a user can silently get a false-clean covenant report' - that specific worse outcome is not corroborated by this trace.

AUDIT_F7.title: No log-only failure

task1_prePreIdentityFailureDurable.construction: A DIFFERENT branch than Workstream H's own test (which mocks prisma.document.findMany and prisma.analysisRun.create - the plain-INSERT/brand-new-row path). This recertification instead forces a REAL prior AnalysisRun row to exist for the identity first (a genuine earlier call to runContractAnalysis), so the second call is mechanically forced down startOrResumeAnalysisRun's OTHER branch - the P2002 fallback / prisma.analysisRun.updateMany RECLAIM path - and mocks THAT call to throw.
task1_prePreIdentityFailureDurable.result: CONFIRMED durable and non-throwing, exactly like the create-branch case: runContractAnalysis never threw (thrown===null), returned a structured {outcome:'FAILED', fatalError:{stage:'PRE_RUN_IDENTITY', ...}} result, and a real AnalysisFailureLog row exists with the injected message. The pre-existing AnalysisRun row from the first call was left untouched (no phantom partial mutation). This closes the gap that the existing suite only exercised one of the two branches inside startOrResumeAnalysisRun.

task2_grepForRemainingLogOnlyPaths.result: Zero actual console.* CALLS anywhere in lib/contract-model/analysis/**. The only 3 hits are inside COMMENTS in orchestrator.ts and service.ts describing app/'s own runExtractionAction console.error as legitimate, disclosed, unchanged defense-in-depth OUTSIDE this tree - not a log-only path inside the tree under audit. No remaining bare console-only error path exists inside lib/contract-model/analysis/**.

task3_cheaperThanTotalOutageGap.question: Is there anything cheaper than a full Postgres outage that could also silently lose a failure record?
task3_cheaperThanTotalOutageGap.answer: YES - a REAL, newly-discovered, previously-undisclosed gap.
task3_cheaperThanTotalOutageGap.mechanism: lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts's own pre-identity catch block (runContractAnalysis, approx. lines 398-402) is: `catch (err) { ...; await recordAnalysisFailureLog({...}); return {outcome:'FAILED', ...}; }`. This `await recordAnalysisFailureLog(...)` call has NO try/catch of its own. If THIS SECOND write fails for ANY reason short of a total outage - a single transient statement failure, a serialization/deadlock error, momentary connection-pool exhaustion for that one query, or (concretely) a foreign-key violation if the companyId passed to runContractAnalysis does not correspond to a real Company row - the resulting exception propagates UNCAUGHT out of runContractAnalysis entirely, past every durability mechanism this fix built. It is caught only by app/'s own runExtractionAction try/catch, which does nothing but console.error it - i.e. the ORIGINAL failure this whole fix exists to durably record is lost with NO Postgres trace anywhere, reproducing exactly the log-only failure mode AUDIT-F7 was chartered to eliminate.
task3_cheaperThanTotalOutageGap.whyThisIsCheaperThanTheDisclosedResidual: 16-no-log-only-failure.json's own disclosed residual requires Postgres to be so unreachable that even the AnalysisFailureLog write fails - i.e. total outage, affecting every query in the process. This recertification's finding requires only ONE specific write (the recording write itself) to fail even once, while every other query against the SAME live Postgres instance in the SAME test run succeeds normally (proven directly: the sibling reclaim-path test in the same file, and every other Part B test file, complete real Postgres reads/writes in the same process without issue). A single bad write is a materially cheaper, more plausible failure mode than a full outage, and is not covered by the disclosed residual's own framing.
task3_cheaperThanTotalOutageGap.empiricalProof: A new test mocks prisma.document.findMany to throw (the ORIGINAL, real failure) AND separately mocks prisma.analysisFailureLog.create to throw once (the RECORDING write's own failure) with Postgres otherwise fully healthy. Result: runContractAnalysis throws an UNCAUGHT exception (contradicting AUDIT-F7's own 'never throws uncaught' guarantee), and getAnalysisFailureLogsForCompany confirms zero AnalysisFailureLog rows exist afterward - the original failure is completely unrecorded anywhere.

genuineDefectsFound: recordAnalysisFailureLog's own call site inside runContractAnalysis's pre-identity catch block has no fallback/try-catch of its own - its own failure (a single bad write, not a full outage) both (a) causes runContractAnalysis to throw uncaught, contradicting its own documented 'never throws' contract, and (b) leaves the ORIGINAL failure with zero durable trace, reproducing the exact log-only failure mode this audit finding exists to close, via a materially cheaper trigger than the disclosed 'total Postgres outage' residual.

summaryForCaller: AUDIT-F3 (partial instrument failure) holds under an independently-chosen, materially different failure-injection point (semantic-coverage-audit instead of semantic-truth persistence): partial success is genuinely preserved, every individual failure is durably recorded even in the total-failure case, and status correctly reads PARTIAL rather than a clean COMPLETED*/FAILED. AUDIT-F6 (live product-flow inevitability) does NOT hold as CERTIFIED - the real bypass the prior report itself found and named 'confirmedBypass' (uploading a document and clicking straight through to Review/Activate without contract-model analysis ever running) remains fully open in the current, frozen code; only a visibility card was added, and that card's own 'view findings' link is itself broken (points to a page blind to ClaimReviewItem). The mitigating fact is that nothing downstream currently reads AnalysisRun/ClaimReviewItem state, so no OTHER page presents a false 'analyzed and clean' signal as a result - but the audit finding's own stated requirement ('a real user cannot reach the analyzed state without the authoritative path having run') is not met. AUDIT-F7 (no log-only failure) does NOT hold as fully CERTIFIED either - both documented failure branches are genuinely durable (including a second branch, the reclaim-path updateMany failure, that this recertification tested independently), and no bare console-only error path remains anywhere in lib/contract-model/analysis/**, but a real, previously-undisclosed, and materially CHEAPER-than-the-disclosed-residual gap was found: the fix's own failure-recording write (recordAnalysisFailureLog) has no fallback of its own, so a single failed write there - not a total Postgres outage - both throws uncaught (breaking the 'never throws' contract) and silently loses the original failure with zero durable trace, reproducing exactly the failure mode this audit finding was chartered to close.
